SM18A-B1.free_elimination: Ledge (480) is below launch height (576), so the landing is after the apex; apex time -b/2a = 80/32 = 2.5 is one mental step, striking 1 and 2.5 (must be strictly after 2.5). Leaves 6 vs 9. Printed numbers: 16 (a), 80 (b: 80/32 = 2.5 is the vertex-time distractor), 576 (launch height), 480 (ledge). 9 is h=0 (ground) but that is not visible without arithmetic.
SM18A-B1.note: Back-substituting t=6 gives -576+480+576 = 480 in one line; Desmos intersection is instant. The stated decision point (reject the negative root; 480 is below launch so only one crossing) is never exercised because -1 is not offered and t=6 checks directly. Standard SAT medium. Repair: convert to SPR, or replace 1 with a post-apex distractor (7.5 = symmetric-time slip 2.5+5) so the apex bound strikes only one; otherwise demote to medium.

SM18A-B2.free_elimination: Sign/band: LHS 8^(x-1) > 1 iff x > 1; RHS (1/4)^(x-31) > 1 iff x < 31. So x must lie in (1, 31) and -59 falls with no arithmetic. Printed numbers: 8, 1, 1/4, 31. 8.5, 11, 13 all sit inside the band and none is an echo of a printed number; 31 is not offered.
SM18A-B2.note: Common-base rewrite is the routine procedure, not a decision point; Desmos graphs both sides and reads x=13; plugging x=13 (8^12 = 2^36 = 4^18) also confirms. Medium on the real test. Repair: replace -59 (falls to the sign band) with 16, produced by writing 8 = 2^2 (2x-2 = -2x+62), which lies inside (1,31) and is not an echo. Key would remain the largest option (rank 4); consider swapping so 16 is present and key is rank 3.

SM18A-B3.free_elimination: Printed: 3 (leading), 2k+20 (constant), 'three times', 'both negative'. Sign: both roots negative forces sum -k/3 < 0 so k > 0 — all four options are positive, strikes nothing. Closure: 100 = 2(40)+20, i.e. one option is the printed constant-term formula applied to another option; an elimination-minded student reads 40 as the key and 100 as its echo. Two-real-solutions check on k=8 and k=10 (discriminant negative) is cheap but is arithmetic, so not counted.
SM18A-B3.note: Vieta with a parameter is genuine hard-route work and Desmos does not hand it over without a slider search. But the item's own named decision point — the sign condition choosing 40 over -8 — is inert: -8 is not an option, so a solver who ignores 'both negative' still lands on 40. Repair: replace 100 (a 2k+20 closure echo of the key) with -8, the sign-rejected root of k^2-32k-320. Then the sign condition is load-bearing and the closure tell is gone. Options become -8, 8, 10, 40 (key still rank 4).

SM18A-B4.free_elimination: Printed: 5, 4 (excluded value), 3. Echo: -20 = -(5*4) is visibly the 'make the numerator vanish at x=4' value and a test-wise student treats it as a trap. 19 = 16+3 and -1 = 3-4 are not visible without doing the (trivial) solve. No sign bound: k can be anything.
SM18A-B4.note: Identical denominators make this transparent: equate numerators, 4x = 3-k, and back-substituting each option takes seconds (k=-20 -> x=5.75, k=-1 -> x=1, k=19 -> x=-4, all valid; k=-13 -> x=4 excluded). Or directly 20+k = 7. The 'candidate equals the excluded value' idea is the intended decision point but there is nothing else to do, so it is a one-step medium. Repair: put the denominators out of step so the student must cross-multiply and then test the excluded value, e.g. (5x + k)/(x - 4) = 1 + 7/(x - 4) yields the same numerator equation without the equate-numerators shortcut; a stronger repair is (kx + 6)/(x - 4) = (x + 3)/(x - 4) with 'how many values of k give no solution' (answer 2: k=1 kills the x-coefficient, k=1/4 lands on x=4). As written, demote to medium or drop.

SM18A-B5.free_elimination: Printed: 3 (touch), -2, -1 (crossings), -6 (y-intercept), 1 (evaluation point). Sign: no zero between x=0 and x=1, so f(1) has the sign of f(0), negative — all four options are negative, strikes nothing. No magnitude bound readable, no closure among -32, -18, -12, -8 (differences 14, 6, 4; ratios not integer). Nothing falls.
SM18A-B5.note: No equation is given so Desmos cannot draw it; nothing to back-substitute. The multiplicity-2 recognition and the leading-coefficient step both have to happen, and skipping the first lands exactly on -12. All three distractor recipes reproduce their printed values. Best item in the batch. No repair.

SM18A-B6.free_elimination: Printed: 10, 11, 'exactly three'. Echo: 5 = 10/2 is visibly the vertex x-coordinate (half the printed linear coefficient), an x-value offered where a k (a height) is asked — falls. 14 = 25-11 and 64 = 25+50-11 are not visible without arithmetic. Sign: k must be positive (|.| = k with three solutions needs k > 0); all options positive. Also k=0 gives exactly two solutions, so k>0 is forced but strikes nothing.
SM18A-B6.note: Conceptually the strongest quadratic idea here (three solutions iff the horizontal line passes through the reflected vertex), but on the digital test a student types y=|x^2-10x-11| into Desmos and reads the local maximum (5, 36) — the decision point is bypassed by a graph read. By hand it is a vertex computation, which is routine. Key sits at rank 3. Repair to resist Desmos: ask for a quantity not readable off the graph, e.g. 'the sum of the three solutions' (5 + (5-6sqrt2) + (5+6sqrt2) = 15), or make the quadratic non-integer-vertex. As written, medium.

SM18A-B7.free_elimination: Printed: 3, -18, 4. Range: two x-intercepts require the vertex g(3) = c - 27 < 0, so c < 27 — one line, strikes 231 (and 231 is out of scale against 3x^2-18x even by eye). Closure: 24 = 4*6 and 23 = 27-4 involve the unprinted 27 or the derived 6, not counted. Divisibility: g(x)/3 = x^2 - 6x + c/3 with integer zeros needs 3 | c; 15 and 24 pass, 23 fails — but integrality of the zeros is not promised, so not counted.
SM18A-B7.note: Plugging in options settles it in under a minute and the key is the FIRST option tried: c=15 -> 3(x-1)(x-5), zeros 4 apart; c=24 -> 3(x-2)(x-4), 2 apart. Desmos with a slider on c is instant. The axis-of-symmetry insight is nice but the vertex-difference formula is routine. Key rank 1. Repair: replace 231 (falls to the c<27 bound and is the batch's third 'wild magnitude' distractor) with 5, produced by dropping the leading 3 in (x1-x2)^2 = 36 - 4c = 16; options become 5, 15, 23, 24 (key rank 2). Even repaired it is medium; consider zeros that are not integers (e.g. 5 units apart gives c = 8.25) so factoring-by-inspection stops working.
